title: Shared unstructured mesh staging model and CGNS writer
overview: A shared first-order unstructured staging model and a CGNS Unstructured Zone writer used by source-format adapters. SU2 and Gmsh are input adapters; neither owns the common CGNS zone-population algorithm. The staging model is not yet the complete canonical Mesh Core representation.
principle: Input-format identity is not an internal mesh model. Readers map supported coordinates, element topology and boundary patches into a shared value representation. The current staging model uses VTK element identifiers and explicit CGNS BC type values, so it is source-format-independent but not output-format-neutral. The CGNS writer owns Zone type initialization, section numbering, one-based connectivity and BC PointList construction. Boundary labels remain distinct from solver semantics until an explicit mapping is applied.
architecture: SU2 reader -> shared UnstructuredMeshData -> UnstructuredCgnsZoneWriter -> CGNS Unstructured Zone; Gmsh MSH reader -> GmshMesh -> shared UnstructuredMeshData -> UnstructuredCgnsZoneWriter -> CGNS Unstructured Zone. Standard Plot3D follows a separate structured GridMediator -> CGNS Structured Zone path.

proves: Gmsh conversion constructs UnstructuredMeshData directly and does not instantiate Su2Grid as its intermediate container.
SU2 retains its source-format reader while delegating CGNS Unstructured Zone population to the common writer.
The common writer sets the Zone type before creating sections and boundary connectivity.
does_not_prove: UnstructuredMeshData is the complete canonical Mesh Core model.
High-order interpolation, periodic connectivity, partition/ghost metadata, arbitrary source entity identity and all provenance survive conversion.
Standard Plot3D is an unstructured input format.
All SU2 and Gmsh element families and boundary semantics are supported.

verification.scope: Gmsh two-quad MSH -> CGNS Unstructured Zone -> OneFLOW native grid.
Checks that Gmsh uses the shared model/writer and the SU2 adapter delegates to the same writer.
